transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you for fitting me in, I really appreciate it. I, um... I hope I'm explaining this right. I guess I came in because... well, I have a woodworking studio, and I've always prided myself on being a hard worker. But lately, I just... I honestly can't see the studio, or really my life, getting back on track anymore. 

I try to stay positive, I really do, but no matter how hard I work or what kind of payment plan the bank puts in front of me, it just feels like it's never going to get better. I'm sorry to lay all that on you right away, but... is that the kind of thing I should be coming here for?
Have you noticed that you don't enjoy things as much as you used to, or that it's hard to get interested in activities, even things you used to like?

Well, I... I wouldn't say I don't enjoy things at all. I mean, I still like woodworking, obviously. It's my livelihood. I guess maybe it's just a little harder to get started in the mornings right now, with everything going on with the bank and all. But I still try to appreciate a good piece of wood when I see one, you know? 

I don't want to sound like I'm just giving up on everything. I'm still trying to stay engaged, I really am. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is.
Have you been feeling down or sad most of the day, even when you're working on things you usually enjoy?

I mean, I wouldn't say I'm sad all the time. I know I have a lot to be thankful for. But... well, I guess if I'm being completely honest, most days I do wake up with this... this heavy, gray feeling already sitting on me. 

Even when I'm in the shop, surrounded by wood I used to love working with, it just... it all feels kind of flat. I find myself having to fight the urge to just stand there staring at the wall instead of getting to work. I try to push through it, I really do. I don't want you to think I'm just wallowing in it. Is it normal to feel that way when things are stressful?
Have you been feeling unusually tired or low on energy most days, even when you haven't done much physically?

I guess I have been a little tired, but I don't want to make a big deal out of it. I mean, I'm getting older, right? That's probably all it is. 

Though... well, if I'm really thinking about it... lately, by midmorning, my arms feel like I've been hauling lumber all day. And that's even if I haven't really done much yet. Even if I've been in bed all night, I just... I can barely push through the basic stuff, like measuring, cutting, or even just returning calls to clients without feeling completely wiped out. 

I'm trying to keep up, I really am. I don't want you to think I'm just being lazy or not trying. Is it okay to feel this exhausted when I haven't really earned it?
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to think clearly, concentrate, or make decisions lately?

Oh, no, I... I don't think I've had any trouble with that. I mean, carpentry is all about precision, right? Measure twice, cut once. I'm still doing all that just fine. I haven't messed up any client orders or made any big mistakes with the math. 

I guess sometimes I might double-check a measurement just to be absolutely sure, but... my mind feels okay. I can still figure out how to put a piece together and make the right calls on a project. I hope that's a good sign? I just really wouldn't want you to think I'm losing my edge or getting careless. I'm still trying my best to stay sharp on the job, I promise.
Have there been times when even things you used to really enjoy, like working on your favorite woodworking projects, didn't bring you any satisfaction or pleasure at all?

Well, I... I wouldn't say I get *no* pleasure out of it. I mean, I still love the smell of cedar, and seeing a piece come together is always... it's always something to be proud of. I still care about the work, I really do. 

I guess... well, if I'm being completely honest, maybe the thrill of it isn't quite as loud as it used to be? Like, I'll finish a beautiful dovetail joint, and instead of feeling that spark of satisfaction, I just kind of think, 'Okay, that's done.' But I still do it, and I still appreciate good craftsmanship! I just... I might not smile as much when I'm sanding it down. 

That's probably just part of doing it for so many years, right? I mean, you can't be over the moon about work every single day. I just hope you don't think I'm ungrateful for my trade. I'm still putting my heart into it, even if it feels a little quieter lately. Is that... is that normal for someone my age?
Have you found that you don’t enjoy *any* activities, even ones you used to look forward to, not just woodworking?

Oh, no, definitely not everything. I... I wouldn't say that at all. I mean, I still like sitting out on the back deck with a cup of coffee in the mornings. And I still catch the games on Sundays. I might not be, you know, jumping up and down cheering at the TV, but I still like having it on and watching. 

I'm not just sitting around moping all day, I promise. I really try to keep a positive attitude about things. I'm still trying to enjoy the little things... that's the right way to look at it, right? I just wouldn't want you to think I've totally given up or that I'm just feeling sorry for myself. I'm still trying my best to stay engaged with things.
Have you experienced days where you just don’t get any pleasure out of things that usually make you happy, like your favorite activities or time with loved ones?

I mean... no, not really. I wouldn't say I have whole days where I don't feel *any* happiness. That sounds pretty extreme, doesn't it? 

I still have supper with my wife every night, and I always ask about her day. I like hearing about what she's been up to. And if my brother calls, I'm always happy to talk to him. I guess maybe I'm a little quieter than I used to be, maybe I don't laugh quite as loud, but I'm still there, you know? I'm still participating. 

I really do try to be good company. I don't want to be a drag on my family or anything like that. I always try to put on a smile for them. That's what you're supposed to do, right? Just keep pushing through and try to appreciate what you have? I hope I'm doing that right.
Have you had several days in a row where you felt down or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, not just every once in a while?

Well, I... I guess I have had a few days like that. But I really try not to let it show, you know? I don't want to be a burden on anyone. 

If I'm being completely honest... lately, most days I wake up and there's just this... this heavy, gray feeling already sitting on me. It's like I can't shake it off. Even when I get out to the shop, surrounded by all the wood I usually love working with, it just... it all feels so flat. Sometimes I have to really fight the urge to just stand there staring at the wall instead of working. 

But I always push through it! I make sure I get my work done. I'm not just lying in bed all day, I promise. I know I need to keep providing for my family. That's the right way to handle it, isn't it? Just keep working hard and hope it passes? I just... I don't want you to think I'm weak or anything for feeling this way.
Have you had days where you don’t feel pleasure or interest in *most* activities you usually enjoy, not just woodworking?

I wouldn't say *most* things, no. I really try not to let it get to that point. 

I mean, I still make sure the lawn gets mowed, and I still fire up the grill on the weekends if the weather's nice. I might feel a bit worn down while I'm doing it, like I mentioned, but I don't just... stop caring about all of it. I know it wouldn't be fair to my wife if I just checked out of everything we normally do together. 

I always try to keep up with my half of things around the house. That shows I'm still trying, right? I really don't want to be the kind of guy who just gives up on everything he used to like. I'm doing my best to stay involved.
Have you had several days in a row—more than two weeks worth—where you've felt down or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day?

Two whole weeks? Oh, no... no, I wouldn't say it's ever been that long straight. 

I mean, I definitely have those heavy days, like I mentioned, but... I really try not to let it string together for fourteen days in a row without a break. That sounds like I'm just giving up, and I promise I'm not doing that. 

If I feel it dragging on for a couple of days, I make myself find a project, like fixing something around the house or cleaning up the shop, just to break it up. I always manage to have some decent days mixed in there where I'm smiling and getting things done. I wouldn't let myself just wallow in it for two weeks... that wouldn't be fair to my wife at all. 

I always try to snap myself out of it before it gets to that point. That's a good thing, right? That I'm not letting it go on that long?
Over the past couple of years, have you had more days than not where you felt down or hopeless for most of the day, even if it wasn't every single day?

Well... if I really add it all up, I guess... yeah, maybe it has been more days than not. But I have a good reason for it, I promise! 

It's just... well, this whole thing really started when I took on the mortgage for my studio space. That was a little over two years ago... about two years and two months now, exactly. Ever since I signed those papers, I've just had that heavy feeling hanging around a lot more often. 

But honestly, that's just normal stress from taking on a big financial responsibility, right? Anyone would feel a little weighed down trying to make sure a loan like that gets paid on time. I'm just trying to be a good provider and make the business work for my family. I hope you don't think I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself... I really am trying my best to handle the pressure. That's a normal reaction to a big change like that, isn't it?
Have you had days where you don’t feel pleasure or interest in almost any activity, even things you usually enjoy a lot?

No, doctor, like I was saying before, I really don't think it's ever gotten quite that bad. Almost *any* activity? No, I'd never let myself get to a point where I just don't care about anything at all. 

Even when I'm feeling really weighed down by the shop and the mortgage and everything, I still make sure to find something to keep me going. I still watch the football game, or I'll go out and tinker with my truck. I might not be jumping up and down with excitement like I used to, but I definitely don't lose interest in *everything*. 

I feel like if I did that, I'd just be a burden, and I'd never do that to my wife. I always try to find at least a little bit of enjoyment in the day, even if I have to force it a bit. That means I'm holding up alright, doesn't it? Because I haven't just stopped caring?
Over the past two years, have you had more days than not where you felt down or hopeless for most of the day, even if it wasn't every single day?

I know we just talked about this, and I really don't want to sound like a broken record, or like I'm just complaining... but, yeah. If I'm being completely honest, most days... most days I do wake up with this, I don't know, this heavy, gray feeling just sitting on my chest right from the start. 

I try to shake it off, I really do. I go out to the shop, and I'm surrounded by all this beautiful wood—stuff I used to love working with, you know? But lately, it just... it all feels kind of flat. I have to fight with myself not to just stand there staring at the wall instead of getting to work. 

But I always get back to work eventually! I don't just stand there all day. I push through it because I know I have to, and I don't want to let anyone down. It's just a little harder to get the engine running these days. That's pretty common for guys my age with a lot on their plate, right? Just needing a little extra push to get going?
Have you had days where you feel like you don’t get any pleasure or interest out of *almost anything*, even things you usually care about a lot?

No, no, I... I really don't think it's ever that extreme. I mean, I know I just said things feel a bit flat sometimes at the shop, but I definitely don't lose interest in *everything*. 

Like I was saying before, I still make sure to watch the game on Sundays, or I'll go out and mess around with my truck for a bit. I always try to find something to keep me busy and, you know, keep my spirits up. I wouldn't let myself just sit around not caring about anything at all. That wouldn't be fair to my wife, you know? 

I always try to stay positive and find at least a little bit of enjoyment in things, even if I have to work at it a little harder these days. That means I'm doing okay, right? Because I'm still trying my best to stay interested in things?
